title: Training Note — Kestrel Auto Finance Repayment Standing and the Card Allowance on Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
**Rule.** On an order under Vehicle Purchase Agreements paid in cash or through an outside lender, a standing uplift is added to the order's card allowance from the buyer's Kestrel Auto Finance history. The history is read from the buyer's Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts: whether any contract is paid off, and the returned-payment entries on any of the buyer's contracts with their dates.

| Buyer's Kestrel Auto Finance history | Standing uplift added to the card allowance |
|---|---|
| one of the buyer's contracts is paid off, and no payment on any of the buyer's Kestrel Auto Finance contracts has ever been returned | $1000.00 (the clean-history uplift) |
| one of the buyer's contracts is paid off, and payments have been returned, but none within the twelve whole months before today | $500.00 (the recovered-history uplift) |
| any other history | none |

**Questions answered.**

*The buyer paid off a Kestrel Auto Finance contract and never had a payment returned. What is added?* $1000.00.

*The buyer paid off a contract; one payment was returned fourteen whole months ago and none since.* $500.00.

*The buyer paid off a contract; a payment on another of the buyer's contracts was returned three months ago.* No uplift: a payment was returned within the twelve whole months before today.

*The buyer's only contract is active, not paid off, with a spotless record.* No uplift: no contract is paid off.

*The buyer has never had a Kestrel Auto Finance contract.* No uplift.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A card allowance of $5000.00 before this uplift becomes $6000.00 for a clean-history buyer and $5500.00 for a recovered-history buyer.
